name: Work Visa — Employed (Cuenta Ajena)

requirement_groups.name: Standard route — subject to labour market test

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a confirmed job offer from a Spanish employer.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Spanish employer.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires either passing the situación nacional de empleo (labour-market test showing no suitable Spanish/EU candidate is available), or the occupation appearing on the Catálogo de Ocupaciones de Difícil Cobertura (shortage occupations catalogue), which exempts the employer from the test.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm whether the occupation is on the shortage list, or complete the labour-market test process.

requirement_groups.name: Highly Qualified Professional (PAC, exempt from labour market test)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a confirmed job offer in a highly-qualified role.
This requires a gross annual salary of at least €41,356.36 (2026 figure, in force since June 2026), processed by UGE-CE and exempt from the labour-market test.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a higher salary meeting the PAC threshold.

evidence_required.document: Labour-market test documentation (unless exempt via shortage occupation or PAC status)

sources.title: BOE — Ley 14/2013, Art. 71.2, Profesional Altamente Cualificado (PAC)
Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones — UGE-CE umbral salarial, June 2026 update

notes: PAC salary threshold €41,356.36 confirmed directly via the official UGE-CE PDF, updated JUNE 2026 — this figure re-indexed TWICE within 2026 alone (January and June), the fastest-changing single figure found across the entire five-country dataset so far. HIGH STALE-DATA RISK: the January 2026 figure of €39,269.92 is now itself superseded and stale as of June — some tier-3 sites still show €39,269.92 as current. The methodology is genuinely unusual and worth encoding precisely: the threshold is set as exactly 1.4× the INE's published average gross annual earnings per worker (Encuesta de Estructura Salarial), so it moves whenever INE releases new wage-survey data, not on a fixed annual calendar date the way most other thresholds in this dataset do — this is a genuinely different update_cadence pattern from the January/July/annual patterns seen elsewhere, and arguably deserves its own national-variable entry pegged to the INE average rather than being hardcoded, a refinement not yet implemented here given the figure's very recent (June 2026) change. Standard route's labour-market test (situación nacional de empleo) is a real, still-active gate that several other countries in this dataset (UK, Germany, NL for HSM) have moved away from — worth surfacing as a genuine structural difference in any cross-country comparison of employer-sponsored routes.
